title: A housewarming invitation that feels like an open door
excerpt: Welcome your people with a personal note, useful directions and enough detail to make their first visit comfortable.

sections.heading: Start with the feeling of home
paragraphs: A housewarming invitation can be as relaxed as your first cup of tea in the new place. Tell guests that you want to share your home with them. You do not need ceremonial language unless a ceremony is part of the gathering you are planning.

‘A new address, the same warm welcome’ is a simple cover line. Follow it with a message that sounds like your household, whether the host is one person, a couple, friends or a larger family. Keep every family name and blessing optional.
sections.quote: Naya ghar, apno ka intezaar. Come over, share a meal, and help us make our first lovely memories here.

sections.heading: Directions are part of the welcome
paragraphs: Your friends may know the neighbourhood but not the building. Include the house or flat number, floor, street, area and city. Check the map pin yourself rather than assuming the venue name points to the right entrance.

A short landmark, parking instruction or building-access note can save several phone calls. Share only the home information you are comfortable giving to the link’s recipients. If you need to explain a door code or another private detail, consider sharing it directly with your guests instead of putting it on a broadly forwarded invitation.
list: Confirm that the map opens the intended entrance.
Say whether guests can drop in or should arrive together.
Mention lunch, dinner or refreshments if planned.
Add separate schedule items only when they help guests.

sections.heading: Make the first visit easy
paragraphs: If a ritual, prayer or other custom is part of your welcome, describe it in your own words and include its time. If you are simply gathering for food and conversation, that is all the invitation needs to say. A neutral design is just as fitting as a culturally specific one.

Before sharing, preview the address on a phone and tap the directions link. Read the invitation as someone visiting for the first time: can they tell where to go, when to come and what to expect? That clarity is a thoughtful part of hosting.
